subject: maths
question: A typist takes 40 minutes to type 4 pages. How long (in minutes) will he take to type 112 pages?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Unitary Method: Time taken per page = 40 / 4 = 10 minutes.

For 112 pages, time required = 112 × 10 = 1120 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 1120.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given:

Work₁ = 4 pages | Time₁ = 40 minutes

Work₂ = 112 pages | Time₂ = ?

Formula used: Work₁ / Time₁ = Work₂ / Time₂ (Direct Proportion)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bfc541c235bc69b9e6f395309138370a89f7d30e9bc9fd40b48eed5d6f0f79cc.png] 

⇒ Let the time taken for 112 pages be x.

⇒ 4 / 40 = 112 / x

⇒ 1 / 10 = 112 / x

⇒ x = 112 × 10

⇒ x = 1120 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 1120.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Direct Proportion

When one quantity increases as the other increases, the ratio x/y remains constant. Formula: x₁/y₁ = x₂/y₂.

Work and Time Relationship

For a constant efficiency, the amount of work done is directly proportional to the time taken (W ∝ T).

Rate of Work

Rate is defined as Work done divided by Time taken. It represents the efficiency of the person or machine.
